resources.string:
Search Assist requires accessibility service for following features. 

○ View and control screen
 - To add service trigger zones 

○ View and perform actions
 - To select identified search field 

○ Observe your actions
 - To disable app when keyboard or launcher is active 

The usage of this accessibility features will NEVER be used for something else. No data will be collected or sent across network

Search Assist jumps straight to the search field of the app you are using. Swipe up on an edge zone and the field is selected for you.\n\n\"Technology should adjust to us rather than requiring us to adjust to it.\"
Search Assist needs its accessibility service to detect gestures and select search fields.
The service is on. Start gesture detection to show the edge zones.
Swipe up on an edge zone to jump to the search field.
Turn on Search Assist, then come back here
%1$d%% wide, %2$d%% tall, starting %3$d%% from the top, on both edges.
• Swipe up on an edge zone: select the search field (and one-handed mode on Android 12+)\n• Single tap: open the notification panel\n• Double tap: lock the device
Changes are saved automatically and previewed on the screen edges.
Swipe up on the edge of the screen to jump straight to the search field in any app.

Search Assist uses Android's accessibility service to:

• Read the elements of the current screen, only when you trigger it, to find the search field
• Tap or focus that search field for you
• Notice when the keyboard or launcher is open, so the edge zones stay out of the way

Nothing is stored or sent anywhere. The app has no internet permission.
